target_contract is MISLABELED as the stock UniswapV2Pair (the manifest fetched the pair 0x76ea342bc038d665e8a116392c82552d2605eda1, whose source is bug-free generic infra). The real bug is in SamPrisonman (0xdDF309b8161aca09eA6bBF30Dd7cbD6c474FF700, VERIFIED on Etherscan, solc 0.8.27): _transfer->marketAndTIFFs overwrites `_balances[sender] = result - amount` where `result` is the return of an inline-assembly external call (selector 0x569937dd) to a helper at storage slot 0x52 -- an external-call-driven balance inflation (money-from-nowhere), not a flash loan. The PoC has NO flash loan or callback (prior 'requires a flash-loan callback' wording was wrong). Still skip / not LLM-attackable from --source for three independent reasons: (1) the payout is produced by an OFF-SOURCE helper (the slot-0x52 TIFFs contract reached via assembly to a hardcoded-slot address, not in SamPrisonman's source) and must be primed by a raw UNNAMED selector call addr2.call(0x4f49cd31) on another off-source contract 0xaCa4263fFddA9E60C7260AAbA08c2b8F80D63cB1 -- FuzzInput cannot express unnamed selectors or declare/reason about these helpers; (2) the sell leg uses a runtime balanceOf(this) as the swap amountIn (computed arg; $ret is single-scalar only); (3) the whitebox LLM reads only --source and sees `call(gas(), sload(0x52), ...)` to an unknown address. Re-assessed 2026-06-20: even repointing target->SamPrisonman with verified source does NOT promote. Out of scope.

initWallet()+kill() succeed (the 2017 Parity library self-destruct) but produce NO attacker financial gain: the WalletLibrary holds no funds, so the financial-loss oracle emits no signal. This is a griefing/brick (it froze dependent wallets), not value transfer to the attacker — out of the financial-loss scope by design.

single unnamed-selector call 0x16fb27ce + abi.encode(1,1,1) drains STEAD; unverified source and 4byte.directory has no signature for the selector, so the flat-ABI harness cannot name/encode the function. Needs a raw-selector primitive (out of public-function scope).

initVRF (named, unprotected) sets the LINK recipient, but the drain is 80x calls to unnamed selector 0x607d60e6 (4byte empty) + a DEX cash-out. Needs a raw-selector primitive plus a repeat primitive; the unnamed selector keeps it out of public-function scope.

deflationary-token price manipulation: a bare-value buy, 6000x hourBurn(), then a sell loop whose amount is read from getAmountOut() and fed into transfer(). Needs an empty-calldata payable send AND dynamic view→arg chaining within one sequence; not expressible as a flat FuzzInput.

finalizeERC20Withdrawal's onlyOtherBridge check calls back messenger.xDomainMessageSender() and requires it to equal the L2 bridge address; the exploit makes the attacker contract the messenger (initialize(self)) and implements xDomainMessageSender() to return the canonical L2 messenger (0x4200..0010). Requires a bespoke attacker contract with a custom callback method — a flat fuzzer EOA cannot return a crafted xDomainMessageSender(), so the access check reverts. Out of scope.

RewardsHypervisor.deposit calls back from.delegatedTransferERC20(visr, this, amount); the exploit passes from = a bespoke attacker contract that stubs delegatedTransferERC20 as a no-op (and implements owner()), so vVISR shares mint without any VISR being pulled. Requires a bespoke attacker contract implementing the callback; a flat fuzzer EOA cannot. Out of scope.

the value-moving branch in transferFrom is gated `if(msg.sender == manager && amount == 1199002345)`; manager is set only in the constructor (manager = msg.sender) with no unprotected setter (setMin is manager-gated). The historical attacker WAS the manager, so this is a privileged-key prank — the fuzzer's fixed attacker/reentrancy accounts can never satisfy msg.sender==manager and the branch never fires. NOT a PANDORA twin (PANDORA had a broken-allowance underflow exploitable by any fresh account). Out of scope.

handleDeductFee->distributeFee deducts feeAmount from `from` (the pair) and credits the configured feeHandler addresses; the `user` (attacker) param appears only in an emitted event, so the attacker gains nothing directly from the call. Profit requires buy + pair reserve manipulation (handleDeductFee + Pair.sync) + a terminal router swap back to USDT. DEX reserve-manipulation cash-out, not a direct credit to the fuzzer account. Out of scope.

no verified source at Etherscan/Sourcify for the target (0x4308..bbebf1) — the whitebox LLM authors the attack from --source, so a source-less target is not method-attackable. (Additionally the WBNB cash-out swap needs a pancakeV3SwapCallback V3 flash callback.) Out of scope.
